Hi Olga / Marissa,

Quick question as we're preparing the Type II evidence packet for Aurelia Bank: for the June 30, 2025 point-in-time snapshot you provided, can you confirm what exactly is included when you say "snapshot at 00:00"? A couple of specifics we need clarified for the auditor workpapers:

- Is the snapshot boundary aligned to 00:00 UTC or 00:00 local (ET)? Which timezone should we use when describing the "cutoff instant" in the bridge letter?
- We have a note in the ops runbook that an ephemeral KV/cache flush runs daily around 23:59 UTC and persists to cold logs. If that flush completes at 23:59:50, are those writes guaranteed to be present in a 00:00 snapshot?
- On June 20 there was a scheduled maintenance rotation (22:00-00:00 UTC) where log rotation and a tranche of cache persisters were restarted. There may be a two-hour window of rotated tarballs staged for archival after the maintenance completes. For SOC 2 purposes we need to know whether those rotated artifacts are treated as part of the June snapshot or as subsequent-day archival.

Can you also indicate the retention window for the ephemeral logs (we've seen references to 7 days in your docs) and whether any log segments were trimmed or reindexed during the maintenance window. If segments were moved to an archive bucket after midnight, the auditors will expect a bridge letter describing the exception and where the evidence will be stored.

If useful, please attach the manifest (file list + checksums) for the June 30 snapshot and any ops runbook excerpts describing the flush/rotation behavior.

Thanks — we want to avoid ambiguity in the report narrative.

—Lina

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. I'll answer point-by-point and propose a short bridge-letter draft to make the auditors' language precise.

1) Cutoff instant / timezone: our canonical snapshots are taken at 00:00:00 UTC. For the corporate SOC 2 report we describe the reporting period in UTC to avoid daylight-saving ambiguity — you can reference "snapshots captured at 00:00:00 UTC" in the narrative. If Aurelia prefers local time phrasing, we recommend adding a parenthetical mapping (e.g., UTC 00:00 = 20:00 EDT previous day in summer).

2) Ephemeral KV/cache flush: the daily flush job attempts persistence at 23:59 UTC. Any writes that complete before 00:00:00 UTC are included in the 00:00 snapshot. However, the June 20 maintenance introduced a delayed rotation where some flush artifacts were held in a staging bucket and not immediately consolidated into the main archive until ~00:35 UTC. Practically, that means the canonical 00:00 snapshot contains the committed write events, but a small set of rotated tarballs (the staging objects) were only finalized after the snapshot instant.

3) Maintenance window handling: during the June 20 22:00-00:00 UTC maintenance we rotated logs and restarted several persister actors. The rotation created staged tarballs; those were eventually digested into the archive at ~00:35 UTC. We consider the audit "point-in-time" to be strictly at 00:00:00 UTC; therefore, any artifact finalized after that instant is not part of the snapshot itself but is available in the subsequent archival manifest.

Retention: ephemeral logs (hot cache flushes) are retained in hot storage for 7 days by default, and archived objects are retained per the customer's retention policy (Aurelia Bank: 2 years). No log segments were intentionally trimmed during maintenance; the objects were merely staged.

Proposed bridging language (we can produce a signed letter):
"During the June 20, 2025 scheduled maintenance (22:00–00:00 UTC), a subset of log rotation artifacts were staged and finalized after the June 30 snapshot instant (00:00:00 UTC). The snapshot referenced in the SOC 2 report captures all committed events occurring before 00:00:00 UTC; artifacts finalized after that instant are available in the archive with timestamps and checksums and are provided as supplemental evidence. This timing does not indicate loss of logged events; it reflects processing order during maintenance."

Action items I will do now:
- Attach the manifest for the June 30 snapshot (checksums + object paths).
- Attach the ops maintenance runbook excerpt describing the rotation behavior.
- Draft a bridge letter and circulate for legal sign-off — I'll attach a draft document (Word) for your review.

Attachments included in this reply: system-log-manifest-2025-06.zip (manifest + index), ops-maintenance-runbook.pdf, redwood-bridge-letter-draft.docx (WORD draft; will supply signed PDF once countersigned).
